summary: Bounded static adversarial review by actual Claude Opus (claude-opus-5-5) of ONLY the four-path Rust compaction-head change in PR77 (product commit 0d3fdc54, Rust tree afc41fcb, checkout HEAD 04c7d22). This was a static read; nothing was executed. Inside that scope, the cache schema, exact-PyInt/canonical-byte fidelity, closed-key decode, lock-before-input ordering, durable snapshot+record+cache readback before any unlink, and the retained authority exclusions are implemented as the frozen task specifies. Three defects remain. The first two are reachable from existing receipt and fold semantics and turn a previously compactable environment into a permanent compaction refusal: a stored author with no fact-free member record (01) and a post-compaction HLC regression accepted at receipt (02). The third makes compaction always fail, after the snapshot and record are written, when the StateDir root or an ancestor inside it is a symlink (03). No secret, plaintext, key or record-bearing export path was found. This review does not resolve any existing global finding or hold (DOS-1 HIGH, OPUS03, SEC03, ca01275, Opus3eb, all M2/runtime/physical/Oracle/release holds). It is not acceptance or a PASS for wider MLP, deployment or snapshot onboarding.

findings.description: Static reasoning, not executed. prepare() resolves each required author's public DeviceRecord only from identity_document.members, which compact builds with the fact-free fold::fold over live commits (sync.rs:9257). Receipt admits commits using commit.rs device_registry (commit.rs:2263-2290). That registry takes the device of EVERY verified env.init/member.add op, whether or not fold accepted the op. fold computes FoldResult.vector over every ordered commit, including skipped ones (fold.rs:2048-2056). Consider an author Y whose member.add was skipped by fold: for example a non-admin author (op_member_add returns not_admin, fold.rs:990-992), or a legitimate race where the adding admin's role was removed earlier in HLC order. Y's own signed commits are accepted and stored and enter snapshot.vector. They then become a required slot, local_record(Y) returns team_compaction_head_unavailable, and every later compact of the environment refuses. Before this change those commits would simply have been compacted. Y cannot be removed from the vector and its member.add can never be pruned, so the refusal has no recovery path. It is fail-closed (no data loss, no unlink), but it is a permanent compaction denial that any member able to author commits can trigger, and an ordinary concurrent role change can trigger it by accident. No test covers a stored author outside the fold member map.
findings.required_change: Decide and implement one bounded semantics inside the allowed files. Recommended: source signature-verification material for required heads with the same rule receipt used. Take the first self-verifying env.init owner_device/member.add device with a matching fingerprint from the retained live commits, re-implemented privately in compaction_heads.rs because commit.rs is protected. Still require record.verify(), fingerprint==author, full-record equality for cached slots and verify_commit. State in a comment that this is public signature material, not membership authority. Alternatively, keep such authors' commits live and document why they are not cut evidence. Either way, add a real-compactor test: a non-admin member.add of Y, then Y's commit, all older than the age cutoff, with literal expected slot/cache/deletion outcomes. Also add the reopen/second-compact case.

findings.description: Static reasoning, not executed. The new rule refuses when a higher required slot's HLC is <= the cached head's HLC (compaction_heads.rs:320-325). Receipt enforces per-author HLC monotonicity only against the immediately previous sequence when the store still holds it: hlc_not_above_previous returns false when get(author, seq-1) is None (commit.rs:2149-2156). The protected receipt path never consults the cache. After a compaction deletes author A's data head n-1, which is now only in the cache, a commit A:n with any HLC <= the deleted head's HLC passes receipt, the past-wall check and the store. It is not future-skewed, so no deferral occurs. Once A:n is older than COMPACT_MIN_AGE_MS and is the required slot, prepare returns team_compaction_head_invalid on every attempt. The refusal clears only if A later produces a higher, monotone, aged head; if A is idle or removed it never clears. The cache therefore imposes an invariant that the existing admission path does not guarantee after compaction. A malicious or clock-reset member device can turn that gap into a persistent compaction denial. It is fail-closed (no data loss), but no test exercises a regressed HLC arriving through real receipt after compaction; the unit test only constructs prepare() inputs directly.
findings.required_change: Escalate to the coordinator/Astra for a bounded decision, because closing this at admission needs protected commit.rs/sync receipt changes; that is a STOP under the task. Options: (a) a separately scoped change so receipt compares seq n against the cached head when seq n-1 is absent (fail closed); (b) keep the refusal but document it as a known permanent-refusal mode with a defined, authority-free operator outcome. Do not silently drop the old evidence. Add a real-path test that compacts, receives A:n with a regressed old HLC through receive_commit, ages it, then compacts, and asserts the literal decided outcome.

findings.description: Static reasoning, not executed. sync_directories requires symlink_metadata(current).is_dir() for every directory from the child up to and including StateDir.path. Existing StateDir::require uses is_dir(), which follows symlinks, so a symlinked state root (or a symlinked team/ or team/{env} directory) is otherwise accepted. With such a layout, every compaction fails with team_compaction_head_persist_failed. The failure comes only after fold::save_snapshot and save_snapshot_record have already written new metadata (sync.rs:9262-9285). It is fail-closed (no unlink), but compaction becomes permanently unavailable for that layout, and the refusal is not a prospective check made before mutation. check_snapshot likewise uses the symlink-following read_json without the regular-file check that read_record applies.
findings.required_change: Before any snapshot/record write, validate the durability-barrier preconditions (directory chain type and containment). Then either explicitly and fixed-reason refuse a symlinked root/ancestor before mutation, documented as unsupported, or canonicalize StateDir.path once and then require no symlinks below it. Apply the same regular-file check to the snapshot readback. Add a test with a symlinked state root or team directory that asserts the decided outcome and that no new snapshot/record/cache files exist.
